title: Organization Record
description: A company, agency, department, NGO or other body. Most of the original mdm.organizations fields moved onto the envelope: org_type -> category.kind, parent -> parent_id, website -> url, domains -> identifiers.domain, primary_location and locations -> relations. `name` is dropped when identical to `label`; only a genuinely different legal name survives in the payload. v2: departments, branches, divisions, subsidiaries, teams and C2 units are ALL organization records distinguished by category.kind (company | subsidiary | division | department | branch | office | team | unit | agency | nonprofit | government | school | household). parent_id is the containment tree (department inside company). Ownership between legal entities is rel='owned_by' with props {ownership_pct}. Branch sites: rel='primary_location' -> location. Roles a company plays for you (customer, vendor, manufacturer, competitor, prospect, employer) go in category.role as an array, never as separate copies of the company.

legal_name.description: Registered legal name when it differs from the common name in `label`, e.g. 'Applied Industrial Technologies, Inc.'

ownership.description: Ownership and corporate-structure facts that are not themselves records. A parent company that exists in the system belongs in parent_id or relations instead.

structure.description: Ownership form, e.g. private, public, nonprofit, government, subsidiary.

exchange.description: Exchange the stock trades on, e.g. NYSE.

founded.description: Date (or year as YYYY-01-01) the organization was founded.

contact.description: Main switchboard contact, not a person's contact.

phone.description: Main phone number (older shape; prefer contact_points).

naics.description: NAICS industry codes. Kept here rather than in identifiers because these classify the org, they do not identify it.

contact_points.description: All ways to reach them, any number and any kind (mobile, fax, second email, social handles). The single fields above stay as shortcuts that older apps read.
